title: Astronomers capture highest-resolution image ever of the Sun’s surface
excerpt: Picture reveals tiny plasma whirlpool-like patterns that have never been seen before
content_html:
An international team of astronomers has released the highest-resolution image ever captured of the Sun’s visible surface. Taken by the Daniel K Inouye Solar Telescope in Hawaii, the picture reveals tiny plasma whirlpool-like patterns that have never been seen before (Nature doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10871-3).

The Sun’s visible surface – the photosphere – is a thin layer of its atmosphere where the fluid plasma becomes transparent. This region is known to be dynamic and complex, with factors such as magnetic field and convection currents shaping the atmosphere.

The studied region by the astronomers is a magnetically active area close to a sunspot. In the image, the solar surface appears dominated by band-like and vortex-like structures.

The authors associate these features with Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities, a well-known effect in fluid dynamics in which rippled structures form when two fluids slide past each other at different speeds.

This generates shear forces at the interface, causing minute disturbances to grow into wave- or vortex-like flows.

The vortices occur at the edges of so-called granules, which densely cover the Sun’s visible surface and measure between 500 and 2000 km in diameter.

Some of these “fringes” are little more than 20 km wide and resolving these structures is comparable to discerning a €1 coin from a distance of 180 km.

The findings provide the first known confirmation of Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities on the Sun and researchers suggest that the instability might explain why the Sun’s outer atmosphere gets so hot, and why magnetic energy builds up and moves around the surface.

“The newly discovered plasma vortices impressively demonstrate how minute processes – at the limit of what we can resolve using all available techniques – significantly determine the nature of our star,” notes Sami Solanki, director of the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research in Göttingen, Germany.

content_html_zh:
一个国际天文学家团队发布了迄今为止捕获的太阳可见表面的最高分辨率图像。 这张照片由夏威夷的 Daniel K Inouye 太阳望远镜拍摄，揭示了以前从未见过的微小等离子体漩涡状图案（Nature doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10871-3）。

太阳的可见表面——光球层——是其大气层的一层薄薄的层，其中的流体等离子体变得透明。 众所周知，该区域是动态且复杂的，磁场和对流等因素都会影响大气。

天文学家研究的区域是靠近太阳黑子的磁活跃区域。 在图像中，太阳表面以带状和漩涡状结构为主。

作者将这些特征与开尔文-亥姆霍兹不稳定性联系起来，开尔文-亥姆霍兹不稳定性是流体动力学中一种众所周知的效应，当两种流体以不同的速度彼此滑过时，就会形成波纹结构。

这会在界面处产生剪切力，导致微小的扰动发展成波状或涡状的流动。

这些漩涡发生在所谓颗粒的边缘，这些颗粒密集地覆盖着太阳的可见表面，直径在 500 到 2000 公里之间。

其中一些“边缘”宽度略多于 20 公里，解析这些结构相当于从 180 公里的距离辨别一枚 1 欧元的硬币。

这些发现首次证实了太阳上的开尔文-亥姆霍兹不稳定性，研究人员认为这种不稳定性可能解释了为什么太阳的外层大气变得如此热，以及为什么磁能在表面积聚并移动。

德国哥廷根马克斯·普朗克太阳系研究所所长萨米·索兰基指出：“新发现的等离子体涡旋令人印象深刻地证明，在我们使用所有可用技术所能解决的极限范围内，微小过程如何显着决定我们恒星的性质。”
